title: Signed cone boundary and descent for functor rows exact on injectives
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal C$ an abelian category with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian, def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $S,F,G:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $u:S\to F$ and $v:F\to G$ be natural transformations with $vu=0$. Assume $0\to S(J)\xrightarrow{u_J}F(J)\xrightarrow{v_J}G(J)\to0$ is short exact for every injective $J$. Use bounded-below derived functors and their units [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] and the cone convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a bounded-below injective complex $I$, apply the functors termwise and set $P_I=\operatorname{Cone}(u_I)$, $q_I:P_I\to G(I)$, $q_I(b,a)=v_I(b)$. Thus $d(b,a)=(db+u_I(a),-da)$. $q_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The roofs $(-\operatorname{pr}_{S(I)})q_I^{-1}$ descend, by the right-derived-unit identifications, to a natural transformation $RG\to RS[1]$ on $D^+(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], independent of the injective representative. Its cohomology maps are exactly the natural transformations normalized by the injective snake boundary in [lem-pur-derived-injective-boundary]. Explicitly, for every integer $n$, every cocycle $c\in G(I)^n$ and every lift $b\in F(I)^n$ of $c$, the unique $a\in S(I)^{n+1}$ with $u_I(a)=db$ is a cocycle and
$$H^n((-\operatorname{pr}_{S(I)})q_I^{-1})([c])=[a].$$
This formula is independent of the lift and of the cocycle representative, and is $A$-linear, with the positive sign displayed. For a chain map $h:I\to I'$, the induced cone map $(b,a)\mapsto(F(h)b,S(h)a)$ commutes with $q_I$ and negative projection, and the cohomology boundary square commutes. The resulting comparisons and boundary squares depend only on the homotopy class of $h$; every derived morphism between the represented objects has such a representative, uniquely up to homotopy. They are therefore natural for every morphism of $D^+(\mathcal C)$ and for changes of injective resolution.

proof.text: For each integer $r$, $I^r$ is injective, so the assumed row evaluated at $I^r$ is short exact. Naturality of $u,v$ makes these rows a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to S(I)\to F(I)\to G(I)\to0$. Additivity preserves zero objects, hence all three complexes and $P_I$ are bounded below. The cone differential is the displayed one by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $d_Gq_I(b,a)=v(db)=q_Id(b,a)$ since $vu=0$. Apply [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] to this exact row: its canonical map is precisely $q_I$, so $q_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $\beta_I=(-\operatorname{pr}_{S(I)})q_I^{-1}$ is defined in $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$.

Let $c\in G(I)^n$ be closed. Surjectivity of $v^n$ gives $b$ with $v(b)=c$. Then $v(db)=dc=0$, so exactness and injectivity of $u^{n+1}$ give a unique $a$ with $u(a)=db$. Since $u(da)=d^2b=0$, $da=0$. The element $(b,-a)\in P_I^n$ is closed: $d(b,-a)=(db-u(a),da)=0$. It maps to $c$ under $q_I$, and to $a$ under negative projection. Since $H^n(q_I)$ is invertible, $H^n(\beta_I)[c]=[a]$ under $H^n(S(I)[1])=H^{n+1}(S(I))$. This proves the positive sign directly.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, negative projection; explicit module chase

proof.text: If $b$ is replaced by $b+u(t)$, the unique $a$ is replaced by $a+dt$, so its class is unchanged. If $c$ is replaced by $c+de$, lift $e$ to $f\in F(I)^{n-1}$ and replace $b$ by $b+df$; its differential and hence $a$ are unchanged. Combining this with the first observation handles every possible lift. Lifts $b+b\prime$ and $\lambda b$ show additivity and $A$-linearity. For the snake boundary of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], use the diagram in Tag 0117: lift $[c]$ from $G(I)^n/\operatorname{im}d$ to $[b]$ in $F(I)^n/\operatorname{im}d$, take its vertical image $db$, and lift that through $u$ to the cycle $a$. Its image in $H^{n+1}(S(I))$ is $[a]$. Thus the cone boundary agrees with that snake boundary, without assuming a splitting of the module row.

source.place: Tag 0117, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, snake diagram and its lift chase

proof.text: For a chain map $h:I\to I\prime$, define $C_h(b,a)=(F(h)b,S(h)a)$. Commutation with differentials follows from the chain-map identities and $F(h)u=u\prime S(h)$. Naturality of $v$ gives $q_{I\prime}C_h=G(h)q_I$; projection gives $(-\operatorname{pr}_{S(I\prime)})C_h=S(h)[1](-\operatorname{pr}_{S(I)})$. Invert the two $q$ maps in the derived category to obtain $S(h)[1]\beta_I=\beta_{I\prime}G(h)$. Taking cohomology gives the boundary square. If $h-h\prime=dk+kd$, [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology] applies to each of $S,F,G$. In fact the cone maps themselves are homotopic via $H(b,a)=(F(k)b,-S(k)a)$: $dH+Hd=C_h-C_{h\prime}$, with cross terms cancelling by naturality of $u$ at $k$. All quotient, projection and induced boundary squares therefore depend only on the homotopy class.

source.place: Tag 014Z, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, functorial cone calculation; Tag 014X, homotopies

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], choose for each $K\in D^+(\mathcal C)$ an injective complex $I_K$ and $e_K:QI_K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$; these complexes are K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], for every $f:K\to L$ there is a chain map $h:I_K\to I_L$ with $Qh=e_L^{-1}fe_K$, uniquely up to homotopy. For $T=S,G$ write $c_{T,K}=RT(e_K)\alpha_{T,I_K}:Q(TI_K)\xrightarrow{\sim}RT(K)$; the units are invertible here by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Their naturality gives $RT(f)c_{T,K}=c_{T,L}Q(T h)$. Define $\beta_K=c_{S,K}[1]\beta_{I_K}c_{G,K}^{-1}$. Substituting the two unit identities and the square of Step 4 proves $RS(f)[1]\beta_K=\beta_L RG(f)$, hence $\beta:RG\to RS[1]$ is natural for every derived morphism.

For another representative $e\prime:QI\prime\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, apply the same Hom bijection to $(e\prime)^{-1}e_K$. The resulting chain map is a homotopy equivalence: lift its inverse by the bijection and use injectivity of that bijection to identify both composites with identities up to homotopy. The unit naturality and Step 4 with $f=1_K$ show that transport of $\beta_{I\prime}$ is exactly $\beta_K$. Thus the construction is independent of representatives, including specified resolution comparisons. By [lem-pur-derived-injective-boundary], the normalized cohomology transformations are the snake boundaries under these same derived-unit comparisons. Step 3 identifies our cohomology maps with those boundaries on every injective model. For each $K$, conjugation by the invertible comparisons proves equality with the normalized transformation at $K$. The equality is therefore an equality of natural transformations in every integer degree.
